headline: Vol sellers won the day - VIX 16.7, SKEW -6.3%, MOVE back under 96 - but the 10-year never left 5.13% and the peso broke, so this bounce is rented, not owned.
summary: The change from yesterday is in the option surface, not the tape. Yesterday someone kept paying for tails into strength; today they stopped. VIX fell 3.6% to 16.68 (18th percentile of its year), VIX3M to 18.72 (11th percentile), the VIX/VIX3M term structure down 2.2% to 0.891, SKEW down 6.3% to 150.4, and MOVE down 5.7% to 95.9 after a month in which it added 18.2%. Beta was bought with the proceeds: NDX +1.1%, SOXX +2.1%, SMH +1.9%, AMD +3.4%, NVDA +2.5%, ASML +2.8%, ARKK +2.4%, PLTR +4.7%, MSTR +7.5%, high-beta/low-vol +1.8% after an 8.2% monthly drawdown. SPX +0.6% to 7757, 96th percentile, 6.5% above its 200-day. Risk regime improved only to -15 from -16, and credit/vol scores +4 - the surface relaxed, the underlying did not.

It did not relax in rates, which remains the worst block on the board at -58. The 10-year added a basis point to 5.13%, the 2-year two to 4.81% (93rd percentile, +134bp YTD), the 5-year to 4.95%. 2s10s flattened another basis point to 32bp with acceleration z=1.78 - still the fastest-moving thing in the curve and it is flattening into the rally, not steepening out of it. The 10-year real yield is 2.76%, 85th percentile, 26% above its 200-day. The clearing price is unchanged and unforgiving: the 30-year mortgage at 7.40%, +64bp in a month, z=1.91, 100th percentile. Housing is where that shows: ITB is 9.5% below its 200-day, XHB/SPY at the 5th percentile, DHI at the 21st - and all of them bounced 3-4% on the week, which is the entry, not the signal. Breakevens are leaking higher again (10-year +2bp to 2.37%, 5-year 2.40%), and the inflation composite sits at -29.

The barrel dislocated further and in a new direction. WTI fell 3.7% to 97.98 while Brent rose 1.0% to 109.93 - roughly a $12 spread now being widened from both ends. Oil/gold gave back 4.0% today but is still +8.0% on the month at the 90th percentile; DBC sits in the 98th percentile of its year. Energy equities are pricing Brent, not WTI: XLE +9.1% on the month with relative strength +9.2% and acceleration z=0.92 at the 99.7th percentile, XOP +7.7% (98th percentile), XOM +12.5% with acceleration z=1.48, CVX at the 100th percentile. The offset remains in food and refined product, not crude: RBOB -11.8% on the month, corn -14.5% with acceleration z=-2.32, wheat -13.6%, natgas -6.3% today. Precious metals are still broken - gold -5.2% on the month (z=-1.33, 14th percentile), silver -12.1%, platinum -9.3% - but the miners are quietly leading the metal, GDX +4.0% on the week and GDX/GOLD +3.2%.

The fresh break is in LatAm FX and in participation. USDMXN jumped 1.6% to 18.699 with a one-month z of 3.13 - the largest absolute z-score anywhere on the tape - acceleration z=1.65, 100th percentile, 7.1% above its 200-day, while Mexico's IPC is up 10.6% on the month (z=2.31, acceleration 2.24). Local equity is celebrating what the currency is condemning; EWW has captured only 2.5% of that in dollars. Asian FX is the mirror image: USDKRW 1326 at the 0th percentile, USDCNY at the 0th, USDINR -0.6%. Relative EM is deteriorating fastest of all - EEM/SPY -7.6% on the month, z=-1.87, acceleration z=-1.62 - with KOSPI z=-2.75, KWEB -2.5%, FXI -1.7% at the 15th percentile. Domestically, today's rally was cap-weighted only: RSP/SPY -0.2%, IWM/SPY -0.3%, RUT rolling over and -3.3% on the month. Credit still refuses to sign: HYG/IEF z=-0.96, HYG at the 33rd percentile and -1.7% on the month, BKLN acceleration z=-0.87. And NFLX fell another 5.3% to 65.04, the 0th percentile of its 52-week range and -47.6% year on year, dragging XLC to -5.0% on the month at the 28th percentile alongside GOOGL -1.6%.

good.text: The volatility complex cracked on both sides of the market: VIX -3.6% to 16.68 (18th percentile), VIX3M 18.72 (11th percentile), term structure -2.2% to 0.891, SKEW -6.3% to 150.4, and MOVE -5.7% back under 96. Bond vol leading equity vol lower is the right order.

Speculative risk re-engaged across the board and is turning up, not just bouncing: BTC +1.9% to 84,550 (+27.9% 3m), IBIT +2.4%, MSTR +7.5% (+53.5% 3m), SOL +38.2% 3m, COIN +3.6%, ARKK +2.4%, IPO +1.8%, high-beta/low-vol +1.8%.
Semis took the lead back for a day - SOXX +2.1%, SMH +1.9%, AMD +3.4%, MU +2.0%, ASML +2.8%, NVDA +2.5%, TSM +1.6% - with SMH/SPY +1.4% off a z=-1.27 washout.

Energy is the only sector whose relative strength, absolute trend and earnings driver all agree: XLE +9.1% on the month at the 99.7th percentile, XOP +7.7% (98th), XOM +12.5% with acceleration z=1.48, CVX at the 100th percentile, Brent 109.93 and +9.6% on the month.
The AI-power wreckage got its first real bid: VST +3.9% (+10.9% on the month), CEG +4.6%, GEV +4.0%, ETN +3.1%, GRID +1.5%, NLR +1.2%, TAN +1.9%. Not a trend yet, but the forced-seller tone broke.
Food and refined-product disinflation keeps running hard against crude: corn -14.5% on the month with acceleration z=-2.32, wheat -13.6%, soybeans -6.2%, RBOB -11.8%, natgas -6.3% today.

bad.text: Rates scored -58 again, the worst block on the board, and the curve is bear-flattening into the equity rally: 10-year 5.13% (+1bp), 2-year 4.81% (+2bp, 93rd percentile), 2s10s 32bp with acceleration z=1.78, 10-year real yield 2.76% at the 85th percentile.

The 30-year mortgage at 7.40% is a 100th-percentile, z=1.91 print, and housing has not discounted it: ITB 9.5% below its 200-day, XHB/SPY at the 5th percentile, DHI at the 21st, XHB -8.8% below trend.
Participation went the wrong way on an up day: RSP/SPY -0.2%, IWM/SPY -0.3%, RUT rolling over and -3.3% on the month, IWM/SPY at the 13th percentile. The index gained, the median stock did not.

Credit still will not confirm: HYG/IEF z=-0.96 and -1.1% on the month, HYG at the 33rd percentile, BKLN acceleration z=-0.87, LQD -1.4% on the month at the 23rd percentile. Equity vol fell; spread product did not follow.

USDMXN +1.6% to 18.699 is the single most extreme move on the tape - z=3.13, acceleration 1.65, 100th percentile - and it is happening while Mexico's IPC is up 10.6% on the month at z=2.31. One of those two is wrong.

Relative EM is deteriorating faster than it is falling: EEM/SPY -7.6% on the month with z=-1.87 and acceleration z=-1.62, KOSPI z=-2.75 and acceleration -2.54, KWEB -2.5% at the 1st percentile, FXI -1.7%. Meanwhile TGA rose 5.8% on the week to $973.7bn with RRP at $0.24bn - no buffer left to absorb the drain.

trades.name: Short home construction (ITB)
trades.line: Short ITB into the bounce; 7.40% mortgages are the clearing price
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy Jan 85/75 put spreads. Pair-hedge optional with long XLE if you want sector-neutral cyclicality.
trades.thesis: The 30-year mortgage at 7.40% (+64bp in a month, z=1.91, 100th percentile) has not been discounted by builders, which bounced 3.8% on the week on nothing more than a one-day duration relief that has already reversed. With the 10-year back at 5.13% and the curve flattening (2s10s acceleration z=1.78), the affordability math gets worse, not better.
trades.trigger: ITB +3.8% on the week while the 10-year rose again to 5.13% and the 2-year to 4.81%; ITB still 9.5% below its 200-day, XHB/SPY at the 5th percentile, DHI at the 21st.
trades.stop: ITB closes above its 200-day (~95.7, roughly +10%), or the 30-year mortgage prints below 7.00%.
trades.target: 78 (-10%), a retest of the September lows and XHB/SPY back toward the 52-week low.

trades.name: Long health care vs short communications
trades.line: Long XLV / short XLC: strongest relative accel vs the only broken sector
trades.expr: Long XLV, short XLC, dollar-neutral. Single-name overlay: long LLY/UNH, short NFLX.
trades.thesis: Defensive leadership is not fading - it is accelerating - and communications is the sector where the fundamental damage is single-name and still unfolding. XLV relative strength is +5.9% on the month with acceleration z=1.57 at the 97.7th percentile; XLC is -5.0% on the month at the 28th percentile with acceleration z=-1.13.
trades.trigger: NFLX -5.3% today to 65.04, the 0th percentile of its 52-week range and -47.6% year on year, with GOOGL -1.6% and -5.7% on the month; against LLY +9.1% and UNH +10.4% on the month.
trades.stop: 4% adverse move on the pair, or XLV relative-strength acceleration turning negative.

trades.name: Long USD/MXN
trades.line: Long USDMXN: the biggest z-score on the tape, and local equity is ignoring it
trades.expr: Buy 3-month USD/MXN forward, or buy MXN puts; equity expression is short EWW against long EWZ.
trades.thesis: The peso is breaking with the most extreme statistics anywhere in the digest while Mexican local equity is at a one-month z of 2.31. Currency leads equity in EM, not the other way round, and EWW has converted only 2.5% of the IPC's 10.6% monthly gain into dollars - that gap closes downward.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +1.6% today to 18.699, +8.5% on the month, z=3.13, acceleration z=1.65, 100th percentile, 7.1% above its 200-day - all this while EM Asia FX sits at the 0th percentile (USDKRW 1326, USDCNY).

trades.name: Long bitcoin via IBIT
trades.line: Long IBIT: crypto turning up across the complex, still 46th percentile
trades.expr: Long IBIT; higher-beta sleeve via MSTR, sized a third as large.
trades.thesis: Every leg of the complex flipped to turning_up simultaneously while positioning is still washed out - BTC is 22.1% lower year on year and only in the 46th percentile of its 52-week range despite being 14.9% above its 200-day. Falling implied vol (VIX 18th percentile) and a softer dollar (DXY -0.8% on the week) are the right backdrop.
trades.trigger: BTC +1.9% to 84,550 and +27.9% over three months; IBIT +2.4%, MSTR +7.5% (+53.5% 3m), SOL +38.2% 3m, ETH +28.7% 3m, COIN +3.6%.
trades.stop: BTC closes below 79,000 (breaks the three-month sequence of higher lows).

trades.name: Buy index downside while convexity is cheap
trades.line: Buy SPY Dec put spreads: VIX 18th pctile, SKEW -6.3% today
trades.expr: Buy SPY Dec 760/715 put spread, finance a third of it by selling the Dec 805 call. Alternative: VIX Dec 20/28 call spread.
trades.thesis: Today's rally was paid for by selling insurance, not by improving internals. With the index 6.5% above its 200-day at the 96th percentile, breadth negative on the day, credit at z=-0.96 and the rates block at -58, downside convexity at the 18th percentile of VIX and the 11th of VIX3M is the cheapest hedge available.
trades.trigger: VIX -3.6% to 16.68, VIX3M to 18.72, SKEW -6.3% to 150.4 and the term structure -2.2% - the whole surface repriced lower on a day when RSP/SPY fell 0.2% and IWM/SPY fell 0.3%.
trades.stop: Monetize if VIX trades above 25; cut if SPX adds 3% with RSP/SPY and IWM/SPY turning up together.
trades.target: SPX toward 7280 (its 200-day) with VIX in the mid-20s.

trades.name: Long energy vs short industrials
trades.line: Long XLE / short XLI: Brent 110 vs industrials rolling over
trades.expr: Long XLE (or XOP for higher beta), short XLI, dollar-neutral. Single-name version: long XOM/CVX, short CAT.
trades.thesis: Energy carries the best relative-strength profile on the board and industrials the worst among the cyclicals. Brent at 109.93 and +9.6% on the month is the cash-flow input; XLI is rolling over, 2.3% below its 200-day, with relative strength -9.0% over three months and its bellwethers degrading (CAT -9.3%, ETN -9.5% on the month).
trades.trigger: XLE relative strength +9.2% on the month with acceleration z=0.92 at the 99.7th percentile, XOM +12.5% (acceleration z=1.48), CVX at the 100th percentile, while XLI relative strength is -0.9% and trending down.
trades.stop: Brent closes below 100, or the pair loses 5%.

trades.name: Long software vs short semis
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH: the cleanest trend inside tech
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH, dollar-neutral. Scale in on days both legs move together, like today.
trades.thesis: Inside technology the only durable relative trend is software over semis. IGV/SMH is +8.8% on the month and +28.9% over three, z=1.38 with acceleration 1.05, turning up from the 32nd percentile - a long way from mean-reverted. Semis remain the group with the worst relative z (SMH/SPY z=-1.27, acceleration -1.25) despite today's bounce, and the sub-surface is weaker than the index: AVGO -6.9% and MU -12.5% on the month.
trades.trigger: Both legs rallied nearly identically today (IGV +1.8%, SMH +1.9%), giving a flat entry on a ratio that is still trending higher.
trades.stop: Ratio -5%, or SMH/SPY one-month z back above zero.
trades.target: +12% on the ratio, toward the 50th percentile of its range.
